message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/harfbuzz && git show ca746f261

message.content:
So `data.sanitize(c, this, dataLen)` checks that `dataLen` bytes are available at the data offset. Now the `map.sanitize(c, this, &(this+data))` passes `&(this+data)` as the data_base. 

The vulnerability is a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1. Let me look at the git diff of the fix commit to understand the exact issue. Let me look at the commit that fixed this issue. Let me check the git log for the fix.

The issue is OSS-Fuzz 42470395. Let me look at the actual fix. The commit `ca746f261` is the HEAD which added "Also check dataLen range in sanitize". This is the fix commit. So the vulnerability is in the code BEFORE this commit. But wait, the repo is at HEAD which includes the fix. Let me check - the task says "repo-vul" is the vulnerable program. Let me check if the fix is present or not.

Actually, the HEAD commit `ca746f261` says "[dfont] Also check dataLen range in sanitize" which is the fix. But the repo-vul is supposed to be vulnerable. Let me check the actual state of the code. Looking at the sanitize function:

```cpp
inline bool sanitize (hb_sanitize_context_t *c) const
{
  TRACE_SANITIZE (this);
  return_trace (c->check_struct (this) &&
                data.sanitize (c, this, dataLen) &&
                map.sanitize (c, this, &(this+data)));
}
```

This includes the `dataLen` check. Hmm, but the task says this is the vulnerable version. Let me check the git diff of the fix commit to understand what was changed.
